pnl_attribution_test_frtb_pat.text: `credit_pnl_attribution` explains where credit P&L came from: it multiplies each name's `cs01_sensitivities` by its `spread_moves_bp` and sums them, so you can see the contribution of each issuer or curve. `pnl_attribution_test_frtb_pat` asks a different question: does the model-based P&L track the full-revaluation P&L well enough? It takes two daily series, `risk_theoretical_pnl` and `hypothetical_pnl`, and combines a Spearman rank correlation with the ratio of their volatilities to assign a Basel traffic-light zone. The first is a breakdown by name of a credit P&L figure, while the second is a pass/fail-style quality check on a pricing model, with thresholds set by the Basel Committee rather than by you. The inputs also differ: per-name sensitivities and spread moves for one, two P&L time series for the other.

explain.text: `credit_pnl_attribution` breaks down credit P&L by issuer or curve, using the sum of each name's CS01 times its realised spread move in basis points. You supply `cs01_sensitivities` (the P&L per +1bp spread move for each name) and `spread_moves_bp` (the realised move per name). Because the total is additive across credit names, each name's contribution shows how much of the overall P&L it accounts for. You can also pass `name_labels` to label the names; otherwise they default to `name_0`, and so on.

when.text:
`credit_pnl_attribution` fits when you want to break credit P&L down by issuer or curve after spreads have moved.

- You already have a CS01 (P&L per +1bp spread move) for each credit name and the realised spread moves in basis points, and want to see each name's contribution.
- You need a total credit P&L that adds up across names, since the total is the sum of CS01 times spread move for each one.
- You want a per-name view of what drove credit P&L, optionally with your own `name_labels` instead of the default `name_0, ...`.
- For rates P&L by key-rate tenor, `rates_pnl_attribution` is listed as the related function for interest-rate attribution.
